components: tree-sitter AST parser (deterministic, local, no LLM)
Leiden community detection (finds clusters and the 'god node')
cross-file link resolver across nine core languages (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, Ruby)
MCP server that exposes the graph as agent tools

commands.text: /graphify query "what connects attention to the optimizer?"

architecture_facts: code is parsed locally with tree-sitter AST, so extraction is deterministic and nothing leaves your machine
it builds a real graph you traverse, not a vector index of embeddings
every relationship is tagged EXTRACTED (explicit in the source) or INFERRED (derived)
you query connections in plain English instead of grepping file by file
the graph can be served as an MCP server so an agent queries it as a tool
Leiden clustering surfaces the most-connected 'god node' and communities
surprising_detail: graphify does not embed your code into a vector store. It parses it locally with tree-sitter into an actual graph, so when you ask 'what connects auth to the database' it walks a real path and every edge on that path is labeled EXTRACTED or INFERRED, so you can tell what it read from what it guessed.
